title: Pelican Packaging — capacity timing
decision_question: Should Pelican Packaging reserve a second molding-line installation slot now, build immediately, or buy temporary overflow capacity?

initial_hypothesis.statement: Reserve a $0.6M 2027 installation slot, but do not release full line capex until contracts and cash support it.
initial_hypothesis.explanation: Reserving capacity is a modest real option within near-term liquidity while full machine capex currently breaches the cash floor; contract overflow and a financing gate are needed.

key_insights.text: Ordering now leaves $4.00M after approved R&D, below $7.0M floor; slot alone leaves $8.20M.
Practical accepted capacity is 9.0M, not 10.0M nameplate; forecasts exceed it by 0.6M, 2.2M and 3.4M in 2028–30.
Existing external molder can cover 2028 and 2029 overflow by volume but not all 2030 forecast overflow or unvalidated specialty SKU.
Deposit is credited toward $4.8M machine, not an extra cost, and does not remove the future funding need.
The 23% growth correlation between prior investment and sales is not causal evidence.
The 98% contractual fill-rate is monthly; annual capacity arithmetic cannot guarantee it.

required_calculations.expected: $8.20M vs $7M minimum; deposit forfeited if cancelled

required_calculations.text: 2029 line contribution versus turning away incremental overflow (not versus contracting it out)

decision_relevant_evidence.text: Five-month outsource lead and specialty qualification
Difference between signed minimum and forecast demand

contradictory_evidence: 23% more sales for earlier investors is confounded by sector and contracts
Nameplate utilization vs accepted-unit practical capacity
Contribution per incremental sale vs outsourced premium are different metrics

reasoning_traps.text: Claiming the $0.6M deposit fixes future financing
Counting deposit twice in equipment outlay
Inferring capacity purchases cause sales growth from peer comparison

key_tradeoffs.text: Preserving investment option vs committing capital
Annual capacity vs monthly customer service

plausible_recommendations.text: Reserve a slot conditionally, secure contract overflow for 2028, and release full capex only with confirmed volume and liquidity.
Defer even the slot if customer demand slips materially or outside molder can meet all constraints more cheaply.
Commit $4.8M now without new financing or R&D adjustment.

defensibility_criteria: Respect cash floor and practical capacity
Plan near-term overflow with validation limits
Set a measurable future investment gate

decision_requirements.question: Does full investment fit after R&D and cash reserve?
Are all units comparable accepted units?
Can external capacity cover the gap before new machine delivery?
What contracts and cash would trigger full investment?
